argument.text: Fix x∈ℝ^n and t>0. By H002 the time section of u has derivative ut(x,t). For applying a theorem on ℝ, extend that section by q for nonpositive times; this does not change any derivative at t>0. H004 gives u(x,r)·u(x,r)=1 for r>0. M001 with both functions equal to this section gives its squared norm derivative as ut(x,t)·u(x,t)+u(x,t)·ut(x,t)=2u(x,t)·ut(x,t). The constant function 1 has derivative zero; uniqueness of derivatives gives 2u(x,t)·ut(x,t)=0, hence u(x,t)·ut(x,t)=0.

At the same point choose a from H005. Dot utt(x,t)−lap(x,t)=a u(x,t) with ut(x,t). Bilinearity and F001 give ut(x,t)·(utt(x,t)−lap(x,t))=a(ut(x,t)·u(x,t))=0. No derivative, measurability, or globally selected version of a is used. The conclusions are independent of the witness a. Since x and t were arbitrary, both asserted orthogonality identities follow.
